algorithm: per-finger MLP retargeting network (GeoRT) trained offline against five geometric losses: motion-direction preservation, C-space coverage (Chamfer), flatness, pinch correspondence, and a learned self-collision classifier
success_criterion: one-trial grasp success (achieved on the first try) plus completion time; not in-hand manipulation
headline_metric: real-world one-time grasp success rate and completion time
headline_value: GeoRT 87.5% / 3.2s vs. offline linear-matching baseline 55% / 9.0s vs. online linear-matching baseline 42.5% / 19.3s (Table III); simulation C-space coverage 90% vs. 38% baseline, motion preservation 0.94 vs. 0.73 (Table II)
human_data: own calibration data (unnamed, ~5 minutes single-user free play plus pinch examples)
note_gaps: the five per-criterion loss equations (Ldir, Lcover, Lflat, Lpinch, Lcol) and the total training objective's exact algebraic form are all unrecovered images; code/md (geort/trainer.py) is signature-only, the loss-computation body is not present in the parse
operator_interface: Manus glove for fingertip keypoints + HTC Vive tracker for wrist pose (real-world evaluation); the retargeting method itself is tracking-source-agnostic
retargeting_objective: learned per-finger neural network trained offline (3-5 minutes) to jointly satisfy motion-direction preservation, C-space coverage, flatness, pinch correspondence, and self-collision avoidance, replacing per-frame online optimization with a single 1kHz forward pass at inference
